[0] [0] With macOS 27 Golden Gate officially launching later this year, Apple continues rolling out beta versions and has now released the fifth beta to developers. Here's everything you need to know.

[1] [1] Apple releases macOS 27 beta 5

[2] [2] Three weeks ago, Apple released macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 4, followed a few days later by the corresponding public beta.

[3] [3] With the official version launching later this year, the company is now rolling out macOS Golden Gate beta 5, continuing its efforts to fix bugs and improve performance.

[4] [4] macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces an all-new Siri app, along with a fully upgraded Siri AI. The system also includes a new AI-powered Shortcuts app that accepts natural language prompts to create shortcuts, plus a prompt-based Safari extension builder.

[5] [5] Additionally, macOS 27 Golden Gate adds new Golden Gate-themed wallpapers and screensavers, while restoring window and app corners to a fixed radius—directly reversing the approach in macOS 26, which adjusted corner radius based on each window or app's menu bar content.

[6] [6] macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 5 carries build number 26A5406e. We're taking a close look at this new beta and will report back on what we find later.

[7] [7] How to install the macOS 27 Golden Gate beta

[8] [8] Here are the steps to install macOS 27 Golden Gate developer beta 5:

  • [9] [9] Back up your Mac
  • [10] [10] Open System Settings
  • [11] [11] Go to General → Software Update
  • [12] [12] Click the "i" icon next to Beta Updates
  • [13] [13] Select "macOS Developer Golden Gate Beta" from the dropdown menu in the top right
  • [14] [14] Click Done

[15] [15] Have you spotted anything new in this macOS 27 Golden Gate beta? Feel free to share with us in the comments.
